name: Amazon Bedrock
pricing_note: Model-, provider-, region-, and deployment-specific token or capacity pricing; selected batch inference is discounted. Imported models add serving costs.
strengths: Broad first- and third-party catalog
AWS IAM, VPC, logging, guardrails, and regional controls
custom model import and multiple capacity modes

name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
pricing_note: Gateway and logging allowances depend on the Cloudflare plan; upstream model-provider charges remain separate. Confirm current free and paid limits on the official pricing page.
strengths: Caching, rate limiting, retries, fallbacks, logs, and analytics at the network edge
supports multiple model providers and Workers AI
simple proxy integration
limitations: advanced limits and retention are plan-dependent
provider feature normalization is not complete

name: Fireworks AI
pricing_note: Per-model token pricing across Standard, Priority, Fast, batch, and dedicated modes. Cached input, batch, regional processing, and deployment tier change the rate.
strengths: Fast open-model inference
serverless, fine-tuned, and dedicated deployments
usage export and Prometheus metrics
limitations: Not a neutral cross-provider BYOK router
model and feature availability differs by serving tier

name: Google Vertex AI
pricing_note: Token-based Standard, Priority, Flex, and Batch pricing varies by model, region, and endpoint. Dedicated open/custom model deployments add infrastructure charges.
strengths: Gemini plus partner and open-model catalog
Google Cloud IAM, VPC, evaluation, monitoring, and regional endpoints
managed deployment of open and custom models

name: GroqCloud
pricing_note: Per-model input/output token pricing and per-hour speech pricing; preview and production catalogs differ. Projects can set spend caps and alerts.
strengths: Very low latency and high throughput for supported models
OpenAI-compatible API
projects, RBAC, logs, usage, and spend controls
limitations: no cross-provider routing or self-hosted cloud control plane

name: Helicone
pricing_note: Hobby is free with a monthly request allowance and short retention; Pro starts at $79/month, Team at $799/month, and Enterprise is custom. Upstream model charges are separate.
strengths: Request-level observability, sessions, prompts, datasets, evals, and feedback
proxy adoption with routing, caching, and failover
Docker, Kubernetes, managed, and enterprise on-prem paths
limitations: Governance and longer retention are tiered
managed model breadth is smaller than the largest marketplaces

name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
pricing_note: Routed requests use provider list rates without Hugging Face markup. Small monthly inference credits depend on account tier; BYOK is billed directly by the provider.
strengths: Direct bridge from Hub discovery to many inference partners
broad text, vision, image, video, speech, and embedding tasks
Python, JavaScript, and OpenAI-compatible clients
limitations: less policy and fallback depth than specialist gateways

name: LiteLLM
license: MIT for core; separate enterprise license
pricing_note: Open-source proxy and SDK are free. Enterprise is annual/custom and sized by request capacity, deployment, and support rather than model-token markup.
strengths: Very broad provider and model compatibility
OpenAI-compatible proxy plus Python SDK
routing, fallbacks, caching, virtual keys, budgets, guardrails, and observability
limitations: Operator owns databases, caches, scaling, upgrades, and security
advanced identity, audit, and multi-region features are enterprise-only

name: Microsoft Foundry / Azure OpenAI
pricing_note: Serverless token, provisioned throughput, batch, and managed-compute pricing varies by currency, region, model, and deployment type; use the official calculator for a comparable quote.
strengths: Azure OpenAI plus partner, community, and open-model catalog
enterprise identity, compliance, private networking, and regions
model router and OpenTelemetry-based observability
limitations: Complex quotas, regions, deployment modes, and naming
router support depends on model subset and region

name: OpenRouter
pricing_note: PAYG uses listed model rates plus a 5.5% platform fee. The free tier has limited daily requests; BYOK includes a monthly no-fee threshold, then a published percentage fee.
strengths: Hundreds of models and many upstream providers behind one API
fallback, sorting, allowlists, data-policy, ZDR, quantization, and performance controls
unified usage analytics
limitations: upstream parameter and tool behavior still varies

name: Portkey
pricing_note: Open-source gateway is free. Managed Dev includes a limited free request allowance; Pro starts at $49/month with included requests and metered overage; Enterprise is custom.
strengths: Routing, fallbacks, retries, circuit breakers, caching, budgets, and guardrails
observability, prompts, traces, alerts, feedback, and OpenTelemetry
managed, hybrid, self-hosted, and air-gapped options
limitations: Advanced governance and retention are paid
open gateway does not include every managed control-plane feature

name: Together AI
pricing_note: Per-model serverless token pricing plus fine-tuning, dedicated endpoints, and GPU-hour options. Rates vary by model and deployment; fine-tuning has a published minimum charge.
strengths: Broad open/open-weight model catalog
serverless, fine-tuning, dedicated inference, and GPU clusters
custom weight deployment and project analytics

name: Vercel AI Gateway
pricing_note: Model tokens are passed through at provider list price without token markup or gateway platform fee; credits, reporting, drains, and plan capabilities have separate terms.
strengths: Strong Vercel AI SDK and web-app integration
broad multimodal catalog
failover, cost/latency routing, escalation, budgets, data controls, logs, and reporting
limitations: BYOK and governance depend on Vercel plan
best fit is the Vercel ecosystem
